GARP: GBAS azimuth reference point (GARP). A precisely surveyed point used as the horizontal reference for the GBAS (Ground-Based Augmentation System) azimuth guidance; defines the lateral alignment reference for GBAS-based approach procedures.
GEN: General (GEN). A broad classification used in ATC communications, NOTAMs, and aviation documentation to refer to unspecified or multi-purpose items, procedures, or information.
GES: Ground earth station (GES). A ground-based facility that communicates with satellites for aeronautical telecommunications, including voice and data links for air traffic services and airline operations.
GLD: Glider (GLD). A heavier-than-air aircraft that is supported in flight by aerodynamic lift and does not require an engine for sustained flight; used for recreational flying, training, and meteorological research.
GLS: GBAS landing system (GLS). A precision approach and landing system based on the Ground-Based Augmentation System (GBAS) that provides lateral and vertical guidance to aircraft using GPS corrections transmitted via VHF data link; supports Category I and future Category II/III precision approaches.
GND: Ground (GND). A term used in ATC communications to refer to the earth's surface, ground operations, or the Ground Control frequency; also used in altitude references such as AGL (Above Ground Level).
GNDCK: Ground check (GNDCK). A preflight inspection of aircraft systems, navigation equipment, or communication radios performed while the aircraft is on the ground to verify proper operation before departure.
GOV: Government (GOV). A classification for aircraft or operations operated by a governmental entity, including military, law enforcement, customs, and other state-operated aviation services; often associated with priority handling or special-use airspace.
GP: Glide path (GP). The descent path defined by a precision approach system (typically ILS) that provides vertical guidance to aircraft on final approach, ensuring a safe descent angle to the runway touchdown zone.
GPA: Glide path angle (GPA). The angle of the glide path relative to the horizontal plane, typically 3 degrees for a standard precision approach; used in approach procedure design to define the vertical descent profile.
GPIP: Glide path intercept point (GPIP). The point along the final approach path at which the aircraft is expected to intercept the glide path from a level segment or intermediate approach altitude; a key design parameter for instrument approach procedures.
GPU: Ground power unit (GPU). A mobile or fixed ground support unit that supplies electrical power to an aircraft while on the ground, allowing the aircraft's auxiliary power unit (APU) or engines to remain off during ground operations and servicing.
GRASS: Grass (GRASS). A surface type code used in aerodrome references to indicate runways, taxiways, or landing areas surfaced with natural grass turf; commonly found at general aviation airports and smaller airfields.
GRVL: Gravel (GRVL). A surface type code used in aerodrome references to indicate runways or landing areas surfaced with compacted gravel; common at remote or unpaved airstrips in northern regions and developing areas.
GUND: Geoid undulation (GUND). The difference between the geoid (mean sea level datum) and the reference ellipsoid at a given point; a critical parameter in GPS-based approach procedures (such as LPV and GLS) for converting ellipsoidal height to orthometric height.
HBN: Hazard beacon (HBN). A visual warning light or beacon installed on tall structures (chimneys, towers, buildings, etc.) to alert aircraft to the presence of an obstruction; also used on vehicles operating on or near airport movement areas.
HCH: Heliport crossing height (HCH). The height above the heliport touchdown area at which an aircraft executing an instrument approach to a heliport crosses the heliport threshold; analogous to the threshold crossing height (TCH) for fixed-wing approaches, used in heliport approach procedure design.
HDG: Heading (HDG). The direction in which the longitudinal axis of an aircraft is pointed, expressed in degrees magnetic or true; a primary ATC instruction used for vectoring aircraft in terminal and en-route airspace.
HEL: Helicopter (HEL). A rotary-wing aircraft that achieves lift and propulsion through engine-driven rotors; capable of vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL), hover, and low-speed flight, used for transport, emergency services, and specialized operations.
HGT: Height (HGT). The vertical distance of an aircraft, obstacle, or terrain feature above a specified reference datum, typically above ground level (AGL); used in obstacle clearance minima, approach procedures, and terrain avoidance.
HJ: Sunrise to sunset (HJ). An ICAO NOTAM code indicating the time period from sunrise to sunset; used in NOTAMs to specify the hours of operation, restriction, or activation of airspace, facilities, or hazards during daylight hours.
HLDG: Holding (HLDG). An ATC procedure in which an aircraft maintains a specified pattern (typically a racetrack) at a designated fix or waypoint while awaiting further clearance; used for traffic sequencing, delay absorption, and approach spacing.
HLP: Heliport (HLP). An aerodrome or a defined area on a structure intended for the landing, takeoff, and ground handling of helicopters; may include facilities for fueling, maintenance, and passenger boarding.
HLS: Helicopter landing site (HLS). A defined area, either temporary or permanent, designated for helicopter landings and takeoffs; may not have the full facilities of a heliport and is commonly used for emergency medical services, military operations, and offshore platforms.
HN: Sunset to sunrise (HN). An ICAO NOTAM code indicating the time period from sunset to sunrise; used in NOTAMs to specify the hours of operation, restriction, or activation of airspace, facilities, or hazards during nighttime hours.
HOL: Holiday (HOL). A calendar designation used in NOTAMs and aeronautical information publications (AIP) to indicate reduced operating hours, closure, or special procedures at airports and facilities on public holidays.
HOSP: Hospital aircraft (HOSP). An aircraft specially configured for the transport of injured or ill persons, providing medical care en route; typically operated by air ambulance services, military medical evacuation units, or humanitarian organizations.
HPA: Hectopascal (HPA). A unit of atmospheric pressure equal to one millibar, used in aviation worldwide for altimeter settings and weather reports (QNH, QFE, and METAR pressure readings); the standard unit in ICAO Annex 3.
HR: Hour(s) (HR). A unit of time used in aviation for flight planning (estimated time en route, endurance), duty time limitations, NOTAMs, and weather forecasts (TAF valid periods).
HRP: Heliport reference point (HRP). The designated geographic location of a heliport, typically the center of the touchdown area; used for navigation database coding, instrument approach procedure design, and aeronautical charting.
HUD: Head-up display (HUD). An aircraft display system that projects flight and navigation information onto a transparent screen in the pilot's forward field of view, allowing the pilot to maintain outside visual reference while monitoring critical flight data.
HUM: Humanitarian (HUM). A flight classification for aircraft operations conducted for humanitarian purposes, such as disaster relief, medical aid delivery, food and supply transport, and refugee assistance; often granted priority handling or special overflight clearances.
HURCN: Hurricane (HURCN). An intense tropical cyclone with sustained winds of 64 knots (74 mph) or greater; a significant aviation hazard requiring flight rerouting, airport closures, and special NOTAMs for affected regions.
HX: No specific working hours (HX). An ICAO NOTAM code indicating that a facility, service, or airspace restriction has no fixed schedule of operation; used when hours are irregular, on-call, or otherwise not defined by regular time periods.
HYR: Higher (HYR). A comparative term used in ATC clearances, altitude assignments, and flight levels to indicate a greater altitude than a previously assigned or referenced level.
HZ: Haze (HZ). An ICAO weather phenomenon code used in METAR/TAF to report haze, a suspension of extremely small dry particles in the atmosphere reducing horizontal visibility; often associated with industrial pollution or atmospheric dust.
IAF: Initial approach fix (IAF). The fix (waypoint, NAVAID, or intersection) at which the initial approach segment of an instrument approach procedure begins; the point where an aircraft departs from the en-route structure and enters the approach environment.
IAO: In and out of clouds (IAO). An aviation weather observation term used to describe intermittent cloud conditions where an aircraft or observer alternately enters and exits cloud layers; relevant to pilot reports (PIREPs) and flight planning for VFR-on-top operations.
IAP: Instrument approach procedure (IAP). A series of predetermined maneuvers by reference to flight instruments with specified obstacle clearance criteria, guiding an aircraft from the initial approach fix to the runway threshold or missed approach point; the foundational procedure for instrument flight operations.
IAR: Intersection of air routes (IAR). A point in the airspace where two or more airways or air routes cross; typically marked by a navigation aid fix or waypoint, serving as a significant navigation reference for flight planning and ATC separation.
IAS: Indicated airspeed (IAS). The airspeed read directly from the aircraft's pitot-static airspeed indicator, uncorrected for instrument error, position error, or compressibility effects; the primary reference for aircraft performance limitations and ATC speed assignments.
IBN: Identification beacon (IBN). A visual or electronic beacon that transmits a coded signal to identify a specific location, such as an airport, NAVAID, or obstruction; aids pilots in positively identifying ground features during approach and navigation.
ICE: Icing (ICE). The accumulation of ice on aircraft surfaces due to supercooled water droplets freezing on impact; a critical aviation hazard that degrades aerodynamic performance and is reported in PIREPs and forecast in AIRMETs/SIGMETs.
ID: Identifier (ID). A unique code or designator used to identify aircraft (flight ID), navigation aids (NAVAID ID), waypoints, runways, or airspace sectors in ATC communications, flight plans, and aeronautical databases.
IFF: Identification friend or foe (IFF). A military radar-based transponder system that enables aircraft and ground stations to identify whether a detected aircraft is friendly, hostile, or unknown; essential for air defense, airspace control, and military operations in controlled airspace.
IGA: International general aviation (IGA). General aviation operations that cross international borders, including private, business, and charter flights between countries; subject to customs, immigration, and airspace coordination requirements.
IM: Inner marker (IM). A marker beacon (75 MHz) located closest to the runway threshold, typically at the decision height point for Category II ILS approaches; provides aural and visual indication to the pilot that the aircraft is at the lowest authorized approach altitude.
IMC: Instrument meteorological conditions (IMC). Meteorological conditions expressed in terms of visibility, distance from clouds, and ceiling that require pilots to operate under instrument flight rules (IFR); the opposite of visual meteorological conditions (VMC).
IMG: Immigration (IMG). A code used in flight planning and airport operations to refer to immigration control procedures for international flights; one of the standard checkpoints in international airport arrival processing alongside customs and quarantine.
IMPR: Improve (IMPR). A term used in NOTAMs, maintenance logs, and operational reports to indicate that a condition, facility, or service has been enhanced, upgraded, or restored to better operational status.
